strengths: Identifies a genuine and important confound in the TA-GRPO evaluation: the unreported compute asymmetry is a real methodological flaw worth documenting
The compute-matched experimental design is sound and directly addresses the stated question
The ablation separating data augmentation from pooled normalization is well-conceived and produces a clear quantitative decomposition (87/13 split)
Concrete numerical claims throughout make the paper easy to evaluate
weaknesses: The scope is extremely narrow — this is essentially a single controlled re-run of one prior paper, which may be better suited as a comment or appendix than a standalone submission
Novelty is thin: the core contribution is pointing out that a prior paper did not control for compute, then running the control; this is valuable but not a research advance
The +2.02pp improvement on Pass@32 is modest and reported on what appears to be a single benchmark; generalizability is unclear
The 'variance rescue' framing in the final bullet is asserted rather than explained or substantiated in the introduction
No discussion of whether the compute-matching is truly fair beyond raw rollout count — e.g., wall-clock time, memory, or token costs may differ
'First compute-matched evaluation' is a low bar for a primary contribution claim

ai_detection.reasoning: The introduction follows a near-perfect formulaic template: one-paragraph background, one-paragraph gap, one-paragraph method, then exactly three bullet-point contributions introduced with 'Our contributions are as follows:'. The prose is uniformly clean with no stylistic variation, rhetorical texture, or hedging. The single-anchor critique structure (one prior paper as the entire motivation) and the three-bullet contribution list are among the strongest AI-writing signals.
